title: Open surfaces with a triangle at infinity

theorems.statement: Let $(X_1,D_1)$ be a $(0,0)$-completion of a surface $Y$ and let $\phi\colon (X_1,D_1)\dashrightarrow (X_2,D_2)$ be a birational map of NC-pairs such that $(X_2,D_2)$ is minimal. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The NC-pair $(X_2,D_2)$ is a $(0,0)$-completion of $Y$. \item There exists a decomposition $\phi=\psi_2\circ\psi_1^{-1}$, where each morphism $\psi_i\colon (\hat{X},\hat D)\to (X_i,D_i)$, $i=1,2$, is a composition of inner blowups. \item For any such decomposition the dual graph $\Gamma(\hat D)$ is circular. \item If $\phi$ is not an isomorphism, then $\Gamma(\hat D)$ is triangulable. Moreover, if $(\hat{X},\hat D)$ is relatively minimal, then $\Gamma(\hat D)$ admits a triangulation which is a chain of triangles. \end{enumerate}
A $(0,0)$- or triangle completion of a surface $Y$ is uniquely determined, up to a unique isomorphism over $Y$, by the set of inner components of $Y$ contained in the boundary divisor.

The following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $T(Y)$ is a well-defined simplicial complex, i.e., every pair of vertices of a triangle of $T(Y)$ is an edge of $T(Y)$. \item Every edge of $T(Y)$ is contained in exactly two triangles of $T(Y)$. \end{enumerate}

Let $(X,D)$ be a $(0,0)$-completion of $Y$. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For every inner birational morphism $\psi\colon(\hat X,\hat D)\to(X,D)$, the triangulation $T(\hat D)$ is a finite subcomplex of $T(Y)$ under the identification of the components of $\hat D$ with inner components of $Y$. \item Let $\phi\colon(X_1,D_1)\dashrightarrow(X_2,D_2)$ be a birational map of $(0,0)$-completions of $Y$ that is not an isomorphism and $\psi_i\colon(\hat X,\hat D)\to(X_i,D_i)$, $i=1,2$ be a relatively minimal decomposition $\phi=\psi_2\circ\psi_1^{-1}$. Then $T(\hat D)$ is a chain of triangles connecting the edges $e_1$ and $e_2$ of $T(Y)$ corresponding to $(X_1,D_1)$ and $(X_2,D_2)$ respectively, i.e., these edges belong to the end triangles of the chain. \end{enumerate}
The adjacency graph of triangles of $T(Y)$, in which two triangles are adjacent if they share an edge, is an infinite $3$-regular tree.
The marking of Notation~\ref{nt:markings}\ref{nt:markings:00} is a bijection between the inner components of $D$ and $\PP(\ZZ^2)$.

Let $T(Y)$ be marked. Then the following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item Given an edge $(u,v)$ in $T(Y)$, the opposite vertices of adjacent triangles are $u+v,u-v$. \item The markings of $T(Y)$ are uniquely determined by markings of any triangle. \item Let us take an edge $(u,v)$ in $T(Y)$ and construct a new marking of $T(Y)$ by starting with $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ for $u$ and $v$ respectively. Then there exists a unique $g\in\PGL(2,\ZZ)$ such that for any vertex with the new marking $m$ the original marking equals $gm$. In particular, $g$ is the class of a matrix whose columns represent $u$ and $v$. \end{enumerate}
If $u,v$ is a basis of $\ZZ^2$, then either $\{u,v\}$ or $\{u,-v\}$ belong to the same closed quadrant of $\ZZ^2$.
A pair of primitive vectors in $\ZZ^2$ is a basis if and only if the corresponding vertices of $T(Y)$ are adjacent.
The identification of vertices of $T(Y)$ with $\PP(\ZZ^2)$ induces the isomorphism of the natural action of $\Aut(T(Y))$ on $T(Y)$ with the natural action of $\PGL(2,\ZZ)$ on $\PP(\ZZ^2)$.

title: The internal Yoneda Lemma for locally Cartesian closed $\infty$-categories

theorems.statement: Let $\C$ be a finitely complete locally Cartesian closed $\infty$-category, $X$ an object of $\C$, and $\U$ a universe classifying the diagonal $\Delta_X\colon X\to X\times X$. The Yoneda map \[\yo_X\colon X\to\U^X\] is a monomorphism.
Let $\X$ be a small $\infty$-groupoid. Then the Yoneda map $\yo_\X\colon\X\to \Psh(\X)$ is fully faithful.

Let $\C$ be an $\infty$-category and $i\colon A\to S$ a morphism admitting a retraction $r\colon S\to A$ (so $r\circ i\simeq 1_A$). Let $B\in\slice{\C}{S}$ and suppose there exists an equivalence $\varphi\colon A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ in $\slice{\C}{S}$. Then every morphism $A\to B$ in $\slice{\C}{S}$ is an equivalence.

{LurieHTT}}] A right fibration $p\colon \mathscr{R}\to\C$ is equivalent to $\slice{\C}{X}$ if and only if $\mathscr{R}$ has a terminal object. In that case $X$ is the image $p(\ast_{\mathscr{R}})$ of the terminal object.

Let $\C$ be an $\infty$-category. \begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., ref=\thetheorem.\arabic*] \item A morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ is an equivalence if and only if $\Sigma_f\colon \slice{\C}{X}\to\slice{\C}{Y}$ is an equivalence. Equivalently, if and only if $\C(T,f)\colon\C(T,X)\to\C(T,Y)$ is an equivalence for every $T\in\C$. \item Two objects $X,Y$ are equivalent if and only if the right fibrations $\slice{\C}{X}$ and $\slice{\C}{Y}$ are equivalent over $\C$, equivalently if and only if $\C(-,X)\simeq\C(-,Y)$ as functors $\C^\op\to\Sp$. \end{enumerate}

Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a map of an $\infty$-category $\C$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., ref=\thetheorem.\arabic*] \item $f$ is a monomorphism; \item the functor $\Sigma_f\colon \slice{\C}{X}\to\slice{\C}{Y}$ is fully faithful; \item The functor $\slice{\C}{X}\to\slice{\C}{X}\times_{\slice{\C}{Y}}\slice{\C}{X}$ is an equivalence. \end{enumerate} If the pullback $X\times _YX$ exists, then those are equivalent to: \begin{enumerate}[resume, label=\arabic*., ref=\thetheorem.\arabic*] \item the diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ is an equivalence; \item the following commutative square is Cartesian: \[\begin{tikzcd} X & Y \\ {X\times X} & {Y\times Y} \arrow["f", from=1-1, to=1-2] \arrow["{\Delta_X}"', from=1-1, to=2-1] \arrow["{\Delta_Y}", from=1-2, to=2-2] \arrow["{f\times f}", from=2-1, to=2-2] \end{tikzcd}.\] \end{enumerate}
Let $\C$ be an $\infty$-category. A monomorphism $f\colon A\to X$ in $\C$ admitting a section is an equivalence.
Let $\C$ be an $\infty$-category, and $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be maps in $\C$ such that $g$ is a monomorphism and $g\circ f$ is an equivalence. Then $f$ and $g$ are equivalences.

{Frey&Rasekh_ConstructingCoproductsInLCCC}}] Let $\C$ be a locally Cartesian closed $\infty$-category with pullbacks, and let \[\begin{tikzcd} P \arrow[r, "h"]\arrow[dr, phantom, "\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}] \arrow[d, "k"'] & A \arrow[d, "f"] \\ B \arrow[r, "g"'] & C \end{tikzcd}\] be a Cartesian square. The canonical natural transformation \[f^\ast\circ \prod_g\xrightarrow[]{\simeq}\prod_h\circ k^\ast\] is an equivalence.

Let $p\colon \U_\ast\to \U$ be a map in $\C$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $p$ is univalent; \item The projection $\Sigma_p\colon \slice{\Orb_\C^{(\mathrm{all})}}{p}\to \Orb_\C^{(\mathrm{all})}$ is fully faithful. \end{enumerate} In that case, there exists a fully faithful functor $\slice{\C}{\U}\to\Orb_\C^{(\mathrm{all})}$.

title: Strongly complete sets and a conjecture of Erdős

theorems.statement: Let $\rho>1$ and define \begin{equation} u_\rho=\left\lceil\rho(\rho-1)\right\rceil, \qquad v_\rho=\max\{u_\rho,2\}, \qquad M_\rho=2u_\rho+v_\rho. \end{equation} A set $A\subseteq\N$ is strongly complete if it satisfies \eqref{eq:L1-divergence} and the inequality \begin{equation} \big|A\cap(\rho^k,\rho^{k+1}]\big|\ge M_\rho \end{equation} for every sufficiently large integer $k$.
Every set $A\subseteq\N$ satisfying \eqref{eq:L1-divergence} and the inequality \[\big|A\cap(2^k,2^{k+1}]\big|\ge6\] for every sufficiently large integer $k$ is strongly complete, and hence complete.

Fix $\rho>1$ and $k_0\in\N$. Let $S\subseteq\Z$ be finite and satisfy $|S|\ge M_{\rho}$ and $\gcd(S-S)=1$. For every $k\ge k_0$, let $b_k$ be an integer such that $b_k+S\subseteq(\rho^k,\rho^{k+1}]$. Then \[ A=\bigcup_{k\ge k_0}(b_k+S) \] is strongly complete.
Let $S\subseteq\N$ be infinite. If $\Delta(S)<\infty$, then $\FS(S)$ is syndetic.

Let $B_1,B_2,C\subseteq\N$ be pairwise disjoint. Suppose that $\FS(B_1)$ and $\FS(B_2)$ are syndetic and that both \eqref{eq:C-irrational-L1divergence} and \eqref{eq:C-modular} hold for $C$. Then there exists a finite set $E\subseteq C$ such that \[ \FS(B_1\cup B_2\cup E) \] is thick.

Let $B_1,B_2,C\subseteq\N$ be pairwise disjoint infinite sets. Suppose that \[\Delta(B_1),\ \Delta(B_2),\ \Delta(C)<\infty,\] and that both \eqref{eq:C-irrational-L1divergence} and \eqref{eq:C-modular} hold. Then $A=B_1\cup B_2\cup C$ is complete.

If $C\subseteq\N$ satisfies \eqref{eq:rational-theta}, or equivalently, \eqref{eq:gcd-tail}, then \[ \FS(C)+q\Z=\Z \] for every $q\in\N$. The same conclusion holds after deleting a finite number of elements from $C$.

Let $B_1,B_2,C\subseteq\N$ be pairwise disjoint infinite sets. Suppose that \[ \Delta(B_1),\ \Delta(B_2),\ \Delta(C)<\infty \] and that \begin{equation} \sum_{c\in C}\|c\theta\|=\infty,\quad\forall\theta\in\T\setminus\{0\}. \end{equation} Then $A=B_1\cup B_2\cup C$ is strongly complete.

Fix $\lambda>1$, and let $\{a_n\}_{n\ge1}$ be an unbounded sequence of positive integers such that \begin{equation} a_{n+1}\le\lambda a_n, \quad\forall n\ge1. \end{equation} Then \[ E(a):=\{\theta\in\T:\|a_n\theta\|\to0\text{ as }n\to\infty\} \] is countable. Consequently, \[ H(a):= \left\{ \theta\in\T: \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\|a_n\theta\|<\infty \right\} \] is also countable.

Let $\{X_k\}_{k\ge1}$ be a sequence of pairwise disjoint sets such that $r_k<|X_k|<\infty$ for all $k\ge1$, where $r_k\in\Z_{\ge0}$, and set $X=\bigcup_{k\ge1}X_k$. Let $J\subseteq\N$ be at most countable. For every $j\in J$, let $f_j:X\to[0,\infty)$ be a function satisfying \begin{equation} \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{|X_k|-r_k}{|X_k|}\sum_{x\in X_k}f_j(x)=\infty. \end{equation} Then there exist sets $D_k\subseteq X_k$, with $|D_k|=r_k$, such that \begin{equation} \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{x\in X_k\setminus D_k}f_j(x)=\infty, \quad\forall j\in J. \end{equation}

title: Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution to the Weak Simplex Conjecture

theorems.statement: \label[proposition]{prop:awgn-reduction} Among all $M$-message codes in the preceding model, the optimal average probability of correct decoding is attained by a centered regular $(M-1)$-simplex whose vertices have squared norm $E$.

\label[lemma]{lem:rectangles} Let $V=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$ be a centered Gaussian vector with $\operatorname{Var}(V_i)=1$ for every $i$. For $r_1,\ldots,r_m\in[0,\infty]$, \begin{equation} \Pp\{|V_i|\leq r_i\text{ for all }i\} \geq\prod_{i=1}^m\Pp\{|Z|\leq r_i\}, \qquad Z\sim\cN(0,1). \end{equation}

\label[lemma]{lem:even-factors} Under the hypotheses of \Cref{lem:rectangles}, let $g_1,\ldots,g_m:\R\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded, even, and log-concave. Then \begin{equation} \E\prod_{i=1}^m g_i(V_i) \geq\prod_{i=1}^m\int g_i\,d\gamma_1. \end{equation}

\label[lemma]{lem:sum-difference} For bounded log-concave $h_1,\ldots,h_m$ and every correlation matrix $R$, \begin{equation} \mathcal Z_R(h_1,\ldots,h_m)^2 \geq\mathcal Z_R(\mathcal Dh_1,\ldots,\mathcal Dh_m). \end{equation}

Let $R$ be an $m\times m$ correlation matrix satisfying \[ R-\frac1mJ\succeq0, \] and let $X\sim\cN(0,R)$. Then \begin{equation} \M_X\leq_{\mathrm{st}}\M_Z. \end{equation} Equivalently, \begin{equation} \Pp\{X\leq c\one\}\geq\Phi(c)^m \qquad\text{for every }c\in\R. \end{equation}

\label[corollary]{cor:monotone} Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:orthant}, for every nonnegative nondecreasing Borel function $\psi$, \[ \E\psi(\M_X)\leq\E\psi(\M_Z), \] and this remains valid when one or both expectations are infinite. In particular, for every $\lambda>0$ and $t\in\R$, \[ \E e^{\lambda\M_X}\leq\E e^{\lambda\M_Z}, \qquad \E(\M_X-t)_+\leq\E(\M_Z-t)_+. \]

\label[corollary]{cor:mgf} Let $G$ be any $m\times m$ correlation matrix, let $\xi\sim\cN(0,G)$, and let $\xi^\triangle\sim\cN(0,G_\triangle)$. Then \begin{equation} \E\exp\!\left\{\lambda\max_i\xi_i\right\} \leq \E\exp\!\left\{\lambda\max_i\xi_i^\triangle\right\} \qquad(\lambda>0). \end{equation} No rank assumption is imposed on $G$.

\label[corollary]{cor:wsc} Let $m=d+1$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be unit vectors in $\R^d$, and let the message $I$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Under the channel \[ Y=\lambda x_I+Z, \qquad Z\sim\cN(0,I_d),\quad \lambda>0, \] the average probability of correct maximum-likelihood decoding is no larger than for a regular simplex. Thus a regular simplex is a maximizer for every $\lambda>0$.

\label[corollary]{cor:mean-width} For every $m\times m$ correlation matrix $G$, \begin{equation} \E\max_i\xi_i \leq \E\max_i\xi_i^\triangle =\sqrt{\frac{m}{m-1}}\,\E\max_i Z_i. \end{equation} Consequently, among all simplices with $m$ vertices contained in the Euclidean unit ball of $\R^{m-1}$, a regular $(m-1)$-simplex has maximal mean width. More generally, the same conclusion holds in any fixed ambient dimension $d\geq m-1$ after embedding the regular simplex in $\R^d$. No uniqueness statement is asserted.

\label[corollary]{cor:finite-energy} In the preceding unrestricted-channel-use model, the optimal correct-decoding probability is \begin{equation} P_{\mathrm c}^*(E,M) =p_M\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{2EM}{(M-1)N_0}}\right), \qquad M\geq2. \end{equation} Hence, for $0\leq\epsilon<1$, \begin{equation} M^*(E,\epsilon) =\max\!\left( \{1\}\cup \left\{M\geq2: p_M\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{2EM}{(M-1)N_0}}\right) \geq1-\epsilon \right\} \right). \end{equation} If $0<\epsilon<1-1/M$, there is a unique $a_{M,\epsilon}>0$ satisfying $p_M(a_{M,\epsilon})=1-\epsilon$, and the minimum energy for $M$ messages is \begin{equation} E_{\min}(M,\epsilon) =\frac{N_0}{2}\frac{M-1}{M}a_{M,\epsilon}^2. \end{equation} For $\epsilon\geq1-1/M$ this minimum is zero, whereas for $\epsilon=0$ it is infinite.

title: $L^{1}$-Integrability of $L^{2}$-Harmonic Forms and the Hopf Conjecture

theorems.statement: Let $(X,g)$ be a closed $2n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with sectional curvature \(\mathrm{sec}_{g}\). Then \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{aligned} (-1)^{n}\chi(X)>0, &\quad if\ \mathrm{sec}_{g}<0,\\ (-1)^{n}\chi(X)\geq0,&\quad if\ \mathrm{sec}_{g}\leq0,\\ \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} where $\chi(X)$ denotes the Euler number of $X$.

Let $(X,g)$ be a closed, $2n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature $\mathrm{sec}_{g}$. Then \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{aligned} h^{k}_{(2)}(X)=0, &\quad k\neq n,\\ h^{n}_{(2)}(X)>0.& \\ \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*}

Let $(X,g)$ be an $n$-dimensional Cartan--Hadamard manifold with $n\geq 3$, and let $\a$ be an $L^{2}$-harmonic $k$-form on $X$ with $k\geq 1$. Suppose that the sectional curvature satisfies $$-K\leq\mathrm{sec}_{g}\leq 0,$$ where $K$ is a positive constant. If $\a$ is also in $L^{1}$, then $\a$ vanishes.

Let $(X,g)$ be an $n$-dimensional Cartan--Hadamard manifold with $n\ge3$. Suppose that the sectional curvature satisfies $$-K\leq\mathrm{sec}_{g}\leq 0,$$ where $K$ is a positive constant. Then for any $\a\in\mathcal{H}^{p}_{(2)}(X)$, $\b\in\mathcal{H}^{q}_{(2)}(X)$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{H}^{p+q}_{(2)}(X)$ with $p,q\geq1$, we have $$\int_{X}\langle\a\wedge\b,\gamma\rangle=0,$$ In particular, the reduced $L^{2}$-cohomology class $[\a\wedge\b]=0\in \bar{H}^{p+q}_{(2)}(X)$. Here $\mathcal{H}^{k}_{(2)}(X)$ denotes the space of $L^{2}$-harmonic $k$-form on $X$, and the reduced $L^{2}$-cohomology group $ \bar{H}^{k}_{(2)}(X)$ is defined in Section 2.

Let $(X,g)$ be a closed Riemannian manifold with non-positive sectional curvature, and let $(\tilde{X},\tilde{g})$ be its universal covering. Then, for any $k\geq1$, \[h_{(2)}^{k}(X)=0\quad (k\neq n)\] if and only if every $L^{2}$-harmonic $k$-form on $\tilde{X}$ belongs to $L^{1}(\tilde{X})$.

Let $(X, g)$ be an $n$-dimensional complete simply-connected Riemannian manifold with non-positive sectional curvature, $n\geq 3$, and let $\a$ be an $L^{2}$-harmonic $k$-form on $X$ with $k\geq 1$. If there exists a nonzero parallel $l$-form $\omega$ on $(X, g)$ such that the operator \begin{align} L_\omega=\omega\wedge \cdot: \mathcal{H}^{k}_{(2)}(X)\rightarrow \mathcal{H}^{k+l}_{(2)}(X) \end{align} is injective, then $\a$ vanishes.

(cf. \cite[Main Theorem]{CX}) Let $(X, g)$ be a $2n$-dimensional complete simply-connected K\"ahler manifold with non-positive sectional curvature, $n\geq 2$. Then for any $k\neq n$, \[\mathcal{H}^{k}_{(2)}(X)=\{0\}.\]

(cf. \cite[Lemma 3.2]{CY}) Let $(X,g)$ be a complete simply-connected manifold with negative sectional curvature, and let $\a$ be a bounded closed $k$-form on $X$. Then $\a$ is $d$(bounded) for $k\geq2$. Moreover, if \[\mathrm{sec}_{g}\leq -K_{0}<0,\] where $K_{0}$ is a positive constant, then $$\|\b\|^{2}_{L^{\infty}(X)}\leq K_{0}^{-1}\|\a\|^{2}_{L^{\infty}(X)}.$$

(cf. \cite[Theorem 1]{CX} or \cite[Proposition 8.4]{Ball}) Let $(X,g)$ be a complete simply-connected manifold with non-positive sectional curvature, and let $\a$ be a bounded closed $k$-form on $X$. Then $\a$ is $d$(sublinear) for every $k\geq1$, that is, there exists a $(k-1)$-form $\b$ such that $\a=d\b$ and \begin{align} |\b(x)|\leq \|\a\|_{L^\infty}(1+\rho(x,x_0)), \quad \forall\ x\in X. \end{align}

(\cite[Theorem 8.7]{Heb}) Let $(X,g)$ be an $n$-dimensional Cartan--Hadamard manifold, $n\geq 3$. For any $v\in C_{0}^{\infty}(X)$, the following Sobolev inequality holds: \begin{equation} \left(\int_{X}|v|^{\frac{n}{n-1}}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{n}}\leq C^{\frac{1}{n}}_{n}\int_{X}|\na v|. \end{equation}

title: Semialgebraic Dimension and Truncated Toeplitz Models for Complex Symmetric Matrices

theorems.statement: Let \(X,Y\) be semialgebraic sets. \begin{enumerate} \item If \(X\subseteq Y\), then \(\dim_{\mathbb R}X\leq \dim_{\mathbb R}Y\). \item If \(X=X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_k\), then \(\dim_{\mathbb R}X=\max_j\dim_{\mathbb R}X_j\). \item If \(f:X\to Y\) is semialgebraic, then \(\dim_{\mathbb R}f(X)\leq \dim_{\mathbb R}X\). In particular, if two semialgebraic sets are related by a real linear isomorphism, then they have the same real semialgebraic dimension. \item If \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^a\times\mathbb R^b\) is semialgebraic, then its projection onto either coordinate factor is semialgebraic and has dimension at most \(\dim_{\mathbb R}X\). \item If \(X\subseteq Y\times\mathbb R^m\) is semialgebraic and every fibre \(X_y=\{z:(y,z)\in X\}\) has dimension at most \(d\), then \(\dim_{\mathbb R}X\leq \dim_{\mathbb R}Y+d\). \item If \(X\) and \(Y\) are semialgebraic sets, then $X\times Y$ is semialgebraic and \[ \dim_{\mathbb R}(X\times Y) = \dim_{\mathbb R}X+\dim_{\mathbb R}Y. \] \end{enumerate}
Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(U\subseteq V\) be a non-empty open semialgebraic subset. Then \(\dim_{\mathbb R}U=\dim_{\mathbb R}V\).

Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathcal{CS}_n\) be semialgebraic. Then \(\mathcal U(\mathcal X)\) is semialgebraic and \[ \dim_{\mathbb R}\mathcal U(\mathcal X) \leq \dim_{\mathbb R}\mathcal X+\frac{n(n-1)}2. \]
Let \(M\in\mathcal{CS}_n\). Then \[ \{S\in\mathcal{CS}_n:S\text{ is unitarily equivalent to }M\} = \{R^TMR:R\in O(n,\mathbb R)\}. \]

Then \(A\) is unitarily equivalent to a matrix \(M_A=(m_{i,j})\in\mathcal{CS}_n\) for which there exist vectors \(x,y\in\mathbb C^n\) such that \begin{equation} (\zeta_i-\zeta_j)m_{i,j}=x_i y_j-y_i x_j \end{equation} for all \(1\leq i,j\leq n\).

For $M_A$ as given by \eqref{1.16} and $D(B, \alpha) = \operatorname{diag}( \zeta_1, \zeta_2, \ldots , \zeta_n)$, where $\zeta_i \in B^{-1}(\alpha)$ we have $$ \operatorname{rank} ([ D(B, \alpha), M_A ]) \leq 2. $$

Let $n \geq 10$. Then $\mathcal{U} ( \mathcal{C})$ and $(\mathcal{I} \bigcap \mathcal{CS}_n)$ are semialgebraic and $$ \dim_{\mathbb{R}} \mathcal{U} ( \mathcal{C}) < \dim_{\mathbb{R}} (\mathcal{I} \bigcap \mathcal{CS}_n). $$
Let \(D \in \mathcal{D} \). Then \[ \dim_{\mathbb R}\{M\in \mathcal{CS}_n:\operatorname{rank}[D,M]\leq 2\}\leq 6n-6. \]
The set $\mathcal{C}$ is semi algebraic and $ \dim_{\mathbb{R}} ( \mathcal{C}) \leq 7n - 6 $.
The set $\mathcal{I} \bigcap \mathcal{CS}_n$ is semialgebraic and $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} (\mathcal{I} \bigcap \mathcal{CS}_n) = n(n+1)$

title: Further quantitative moduli around uniform convexity

theorems.statement: Let $X$ be a uniformly convex Banach space with modulus $\eta : (0,\infty) \to (0,1]$. Then, for all $\eps$, $r>0$ and all $x,y \in X$ with $\|x\|\leq r$, $\|y\| \leq r$ and $\|x-y\| \geq \eps r$ one has that $$\left\|\frac{x+y}2\right\| \leq (1-\eta(\eps))r.$$
Let $(X,d,W)$ be a $W$-hyperbolic space, $\lambda \in [0,1]$ and $x$, $y$, $a \in X$. Then $$d^2\left((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y,a\right) \leq (1-\lambda)d^2(x,a)+\lambda d^2(y,a).$$

{Pru81}}] Let $X$ be a Banach space. We have that $X$ is uniformly convex iff for any $R >0$ there is a function $\omega_R : [0, \infty) \to [0,\infty)$, which is non-decreasing and $0$ is its only zero, such that, for any $x$, $y \in X$ with $\|x\|$, $\|y\| \leq R$ and for any $x^* \in Jx$ and $y^* \in Jy$, we have that $$\langle x-y, x^*-y^* \rangle \geq \omega_R(\|x-y\|) \cdot \|x-y\|.$$

Let $X$ be a Banach space. The condition in Theorem~\ref{pru} is equivalent to the following: there is an $\omega : (0,\infty) \times (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ such that, for any $R$, $\rho >0$, for any $x$, $y \in X$ with $\|x-y\| \geq \rho$ and $\|x\|$, $\|y\| \leq R$ and for any $x^* \in Jx$ and $y^* \in Jy$, we have that $$\langle x-y, x^*-y^* \rangle \geq \omega(R,\rho) \cdot \|x-y\|.$$

Let $X$ be a Banach space. The condition in Theorem~\ref{pru} is further equivalent to the following: there is an $\alpha : (0,\infty) \times (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ such that, for any $R$, $\rho >0$, for any $x$, $y \in X$ with $\|x-y\| \geq \rho$ and $\|x\|$, $\|y\| \leq R$ and for any $x^* \in Jx$ and $y^* \in Jy$, we have that $$\langle x-y, x^*-y^* \rangle \geq \alpha(R,\rho).$$

Define, for any $\eta : (0,\infty) \to (0,1]$ and any $R$, $\rho > 0$, $$\alpha_\eta(R, \rho) := \min\left( \frac{\rho^2}{64}\eta^2\left(\frac\rho R\right),\ \frac{\rho^2}8\eta\left(\frac\rho R\right) \right).$$ Let $X$ be a uniformly convex Banach space with modulus $\eta : (0,\infty) \to (0,1]$. Let $R$, $\rho >0$, let $x$, $y \in X$ be with $\|x-y\| \geq \rho$ and $\|x\|$, $\|y\| \leq R$ and let $x^* \in Jx$ and $y^* \in Jy$. Then we have that $$\langle x-y, x^*-y^* \rangle \geq \alpha_\eta(R,\rho).$$

title: Recovery of Schrödinger nonlinearity from the large-data scattering behavior

theorems.statement: Call a pair $(p,q)$ of Schr\"odinger admissible for $d=3$ if $2\leq p,q\leq \infty$ and $\frac{2}{p}+\frac{3}{q} = \frac{3}{2}$. Then for any admissible pair $(p,q)$ and $(\tilde{p},\tilde{q})$, we have homogeneous Strichartz estimate \begin{equation} \|\e^{\i t\Delta}u_0\|_{\L^p_t\L^q_x(\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3)}\lesssim_{p,q}\|u_0\|_{\L^2_x(\mathbb{R}^3)}, \end{equation} the dual homogeneous Strichartz estimate \begin{equation} \left\|\int_{\mathbb{R}}\e^{-\i s\Delta}F(s)\ \mathrm{d}s\right\|_{\L^2_x(\mathbb{R}^3)}\lesssim_{\tilde{p},\tilde{q}}\|F\|_{\L^{\tilde{p}'}_t\L^{\tilde{q}'}_x(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^3)}, \end{equation} and the inhomogeneous Strichartz estimate \begin{equation} \left\|\int_{s<t}\e^{\i(t-s)\Delta}F(s)\ \mathrm{d}s\right\|_{\L^p_t\L^q_x(\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3)}\lesssim_{p,q,\tilde{p},\tilde{q}}\|F\|_{\L^{\tilde{p}'}_t\L^{\tilde{q}'}_x(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^3)}. \end{equation}
For $u\in \H^1_x(\mathbb{R}^3)$, \begin{equation} \|u\|_{\L^4_x(\mathbb{R}^3)}\lesssim \|u\|^{1/4}_{\L^2_x(\mathbb{R}^3)}\|u\|^{3/4}_{\dot{\H}^1_x(\mathbb{R}^3)}. \end{equation}
The Cauchy problem \eqref{cubic-nls-1} is globally well-posed.

Let $u(t)$ be a global solution to \eqref{cubic-nls-1}. Assume \begin{equation} \int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(t,x)|^5\ \mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}t<\infty. \end{equation} Then $u(t)$ scatters, which means there exist $u_{-},u_{+}\in \H^1$ such that $$\lim_{t\to \pm\infty}\|u(t) - \e^{\i t\Delta}u_{\pm}\|_{\H^1} = 0.$$

For any $u_0 \in \H^1_x(\mathbb{R}^3)$, the corresponding global solution $u(t)$ to \eqref{cubic-nls-1} scatters and $$\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(t,x)|^5\ \mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}t < C\left(\|a\|_{\W^{1,\infty}_x},\|u_0\|_{\H^1_x}\right).$$

Let $u_0\in \H^1_x(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and $u(t)$ be the corresponding global solution to \eqref{cubic-nls-1}. Then \begin{equation} \|u\|_{\L^4_{t,x}(\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3)}\lesssim \|u\|_{\L^{\infty}_t\H^1_x(\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3)}\lesssim 1. \end{equation}

For any $u_0\in \H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$, let $u(t)$ be the corresponding global scattering solution to \eqref{cubic-nls-1}. If $v_0\in B_{\varepsilon}(u_0)$ and set $w^{\varepsilon}(t) = v^{\varepsilon}(t) - u(t)$, where $v^{\varepsilon}(t)$ is the global scattering solution to \eqref{cubic-nls-1} corresponding to $v_0$, then \begin{equation} \|w^{\varepsilon}\|_{\L^5_{t,x}(\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3)}\leq C\left(\|a\|_{\W^{1,\infty}_x},\|u_0\|_{\H^1_x}\right)\varepsilon \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \|\langle \nabla \rangle w^{\varepsilon}\|_{\L^p_t\L^q_x(\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3)}\leq C\left(\|a\|_{\W^{1,\infty}_x},\|u_0\|_{\H^1_x}\right)\varepsilon \end{equation} for all Schr\"odinger admissible pairs $(p,q)$.

\begin{equation} w_1(t,x) := \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\frac{w^{\varepsilon}(t,x)}{\varepsilon} \end{equation} is a well-defined $\S^1$ function solving \begin{equation} (\i \partial_t + \Delta)w_{1} = 2a|u|^2w_{1} + au^2\overline{w_1} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \|w_1\|_{\S^1}\leq C\left(\|a\|_{\W^{1,\infty}_x},\|u_0\|_{\H^1_x}\right). \end{equation}
We have \begin{equation} \lim_{t\to -\infty}\|w_1(t) - \e^{\i t\Delta}\varphi\|_{\H^1_x} = 0. \end{equation}

\begin{equation} w_2(t,x) := \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\frac{w^{\varepsilon} - \varepsilon w_1}{\varepsilon^2} \end{equation} is a well-defined $\S^1$ function solving \begin{equation} (\i \partial_t + \Delta)w_{2} = 2a|u|^2w_{2} + au^2\overline{w_2} + 2au|w_{1}|^2 + a\bar{u}(w_1)^2 \end{equation} with \begin{equation} \|w_2\|_{\S^1}\leq C\left(\|a\|_{\W^{1,\infty}_x},\|u_0\|_{\H^1_x}\right). \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lim_{t\to -\infty}\|w_2\|_{\S^1((-\infty,t))} = 0 \end{equation}
